reason: The cited evidence does not address FeMnNiGeSi alloys, nanoscale thin films, or the role of strain/defects on magnetocaloric response. E1 discusses dielectric properties of a magnetic HEO perovskite, E2 reports antiferromagnetism and exchange bias in rock-salt HEOs, and E3 compares magnetocaloric refrigerant capacity in annealed vs. as-rolled bulk HEAs without linking strain or defects to hysteresis. None of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Interfacial strain and defects create a broad distribution of exchange interactions in FeMnNiGeSi films/nanoribbons.
This broadened exchange distribution governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-field cooling.
Mild annealing relieves interfacial strain and reduces defect density without phase separation.
Reduced strain/defects sharpen the magnetic transition and diminish hysteresis by homogenizing exchange and reducing domain wall pinning.
Reduced defect scattering improves local thermal connectivity, mitigating heat-transfer limitations.
